payload.summary: engine board: resolution 5rwbt08h (dice-and-corridor movement) directly contradicts ADR-0003's recorded consequence that 'Rooms and adjacency are modelled as a named graph rather than a grid'. Built per the journal, so ADR-0003 is now stale on that point and should be amended or superseded. Board encoded as data: 9 room boxes + 7 axis-aligned corridor segments on one coordinate plane, expanded at build time into 77 unit corridor squares and 17 doors (classic per-room door counts). buildBoard() validates its own data: no corridor square inside a room box, every door adjacent to its room, every room doored, every start square real.

engine deduction finding, load-bearing for the game-master/AI-player items: the naive closed-world inference 'if a refuted suggestion has two of its three named cards already located, the refuter holds the third' is WRONG. The refuter shows one card THEY hold, so cards already known to sit in some OTHER player's hand must be excluded, but cards already known to be the refuter's own must stay in the candidate set. The naive form derives false card locations (caught by the engine playthrough test, which then could not finish a 4-6 player game). Correct rule: possible = named cards not known to be held by a player other than the refuter; if |possible| == 1 the refuter holds it. Whoever builds the LLM suspects' reasoning must use the corrected form.

engine build complete: 7 modules under src/engine (rng, cards, board, types, setup, actions, view, index) and 7 test files under tests/engine — 172 engine tests green, whole repo 203 green including the sibling llm slice, and 'bunx tsc --noEmit' clean under the strict tsconfig. Deliberate deviations from classic Clue, all for the host/panel to weigh: (1) ONE d6 per turn, not 2d6 — taken from the step directive's explicit 'roll d6'; the classic game rolls two dice, so cross-board trips are slow. (2) The corridor is a faithful-in-structure, loose-in-measurement simplification of the 24x25 board: 9 room boxes plus 7 axis-aligned corridor segments expanded to 77 unit squares, 17 doors with classic per-room counts, corridor squares hold one token and block passage. (3) Minimum roster is 2, not the classic 3. (4) Refutation card choice defaults to the seeded RNG so replay stays exact; callers may pass a chooseRefutationCard callback to let a human or an LLM seat pick. (5) A suggestion relocates the weapon token as well as the suspect, and a player pulled into a room may suggest from there next turn without moving.

bindings.crit-codex:
codex
`endTurn()` accepts `awaiting-roll`, allowing players to skip the mandatory movement phase and violating engine-owned turn legality.
`chooseRefutationCard` executes an arbitrary callback inside `makeSuggestion()`, so identical state and action inputs can produce different outcomes, breaking determinism and engine-owned refutation choice.
bindings.crit-agy:
1. In a two-player game, dealing the remaining 18 cards gives each player perfect knowledge of the other's hand, allowing them to instantly deduce the solution without playing.
2. Using an optional callback for refutation choices breaks the deterministic "pure function over plain state" architecture, as player input must be a distinct, serializable action to maintain replayability.

payload.summary: tokens build-review/panel: reviewer-codex=98,269 total, reviewer-agy=14907/3211 (in/out); --no-preflight per open first-scaffold obligation

[agy] two-player deal gave perfect knowledge — FIXED (commit 1eebe3d). src/engine/setup.ts: MIN_PLAYERS 2 -> 3, classic Clue's minimum; with two seats the 18 undealt cards split between the two hands so each player names the other's hand by subtracting their own from the deck. Test: tests/engine/setup.test.ts 'rejects a two-player roster: two hands give each seat perfect knowledge of the other' (asserts MIN_PLAYERS===3 and defaultRoster(2) throws), plus playerCount:2 added to 'rejects a roster that is too small or too large'. The duplicate-id/character/non-suspect rosters were widened to 3 seats so they still fail for the defect under test, not for roster size.

[codex] endTurn() accepted phase awaiting-roll, letting a player skip the mandatory roll+move — FIXED (commit ee6a364). src/engine/actions.ts endTurn now throws IllegalActionError in awaiting-roll unless the seat hasMovedThisTurn, hasSuggestedThisTurn (the pulled-into-a-room case, where suggesting from that room is the turn), or is eliminated — advanceTurn already skips eliminated seats, and the exemption keeps a forced eliminated turn from deadlocking. Tests in tests/engine/actions.test.ts: 'refuses to skip the mandatory roll and move' (the rewritten assertion; the old 'wraps from the last seat back to the first' pinned exactly the rejected behaviour and now goes through standingInRoom), 'is legal once the roll has been spent on a move', 'is legal after a secret passage, which replaces the roll', 'a player pulled into a room may suggest there and then end without moving', 'an eliminated seat whose turn is forced on it may pass'. The elimination-skip test in makeAccusation was also rewritten to take real turns. Suite 209 pass / 0 fail, tsc clean.

[codex + agy, both vendors converged] chooseRefutationCard was an arbitrary callback inside makeSuggestion, so identical state+action could produce different outcomes and the choice was not a serializable action — FIXED (commit ed9e722). The callback and the SuggestionOptions type are gone, and makeSuggestion no longer touches the RNG at all. New: TurnPhase 'awaiting-refutation' and GameState.pendingRefutation (PendingRefutation = suggester, refuter, triple, options in hand order) in src/engine/types.ts; a refuter with EXACTLY ONE matching card is resolved inside makeSuggestion, MORE THAN ONE parks the turn and the new action provideRefutationCard(state, card) in src/engine/actions.ts completes it — validated on phase/pending (the turn slot: only the named refuter owes it) and on membership in the options set. Event visibility unchanged: suggestion-refuted is 'all', refutation-card-shown is [suggester, refuter]; both are appended by the same refutationEvents() helper on either path. rollDice/moveTo/makeSuggestion/makeAccusation/endTurn all refuse while a refutation is pending (accusation and endTurn needed explicit new guards). playerView gained a pendingRefutation projection: everyone sees who owes the choice, only the refuter sees the cards. Tests (tests/engine/actions.test.ts describe 'provideRefutationCard'): parks in awaiting-refutation naming chooser and options; completes and returns to awaiting-action; keeps visibility scoping; may show any matching card and only those; illegal with nothing pending; rest of the turn blocked until chosen; 'the choice never touches the RNG — determinism comes from the action log'. Plus 'a lone matching card settles the refutation inside the same action'. The three OLD tests that pinned the rejected behaviour (the chooser callback, the not-offered-card callback, and 'without a chooser the engine picks deterministically from the seed') were rewritten to the corrected semantics. view.test.ts's suggested() fixture now chains provideRefutationCard and gained 'a pending refutation names the chooser publicly but the cards privately'; the playthrough bot resolves pending refutations through the real action via settleRefutation() (first option in hand order), so the deterministic-replay and solvability tests still hold. Suite 215 pass / 0 fail across 9 files (llm slice 31), tsc clean.

ADR amendment landed (commit d9ac7db) — with a correction to the instruction's premise. The stale named-graph consequence is NOT in 0001: 'Rooms and adjacency are modelled as a named graph rather than a grid' is consequence 3 of docs/adr/0003-cli-first-ui.md (grep 'graph' across docs/ hits 0003 only; 0001 and 0002 never mention adjacency). I amended the ADR that actually carries the claim, i.e. 0003, with a dated section 'Amendment — 2026-08-23: superseded on movement' citing orchestrator resolution 5rwbt08h (journal event): dice-and-corridor board per the standard rule set, which is what src/engine/board.ts implements (9 room boxes + 7 corridor segments -> 77 unit squares, 17 doors, 2 secret passages). The rest of 0003 — terminal CLI, engine-decided outcomes, geometry conveyed in text — is explicitly left standing.
